title: Vanishing with a nonunit prime annihilator
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $X,Y$ arbitrary schemes, $a:Y\to X$ any morphism, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, $r$ a prime, and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Suppose $r\,\operatorname{id}_F=0$, $r$ is not a unit in $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}k,\mathcal O)$, and $F$ has torsion of invertible order on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]. For every $q\ge0$, both $H^q(X,F)$ and $H^q(Y,a^*F)$ of the underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] are subsingletons.

proof.text: Map the prime annihilation identity to each geometric stalk using sheafFiber_map_smul. For a stalk element take an invertible annihilator n. If r divided n, the unit product would force r to be a unit, a contradiction; primality implies gcd(r,n)=1. The Mathlib lemma nsmul_eq_zero_iff_of_coprime therefore forces the element to be zero. Geometric stalks faithfully detect equality, so id_F=0. Forgetting coefficients maps this identity to id=0, and inverse image preserves zero objects. subsingleton_H_of_isZero proves the two claims.
